text:
samir: Heads up — the sampleapp started failing for me after I rotated the org-level API key this morning. Getting 401s when hitting /v1/generate.

carla: ugh, are you using the local CLI creds or env var? quick repro steps?

samir: repro: pulled latest sampleapp, set env: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_live_xxx` then ran `npm run dev`. After rotation I set `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_live_newyyy` but app still 401s. Logs: 
```
2024-05-18T09:12:03Z ERROR fetch /v1/generate 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
2024-05-18T09:12:03Z DEBUG AuthProvider resolved key from env: REDWOOD_TOKEN
```
Weird: debug says it resolved REDWOOD_TOKEN even though I only exported REDWOOD_API_KEY.

jlee: ohhh. That's the parity bug we've suspected — Node SDK falls back to REDWOOD_TOKEN, Python SDK prefers REDWOOD_API_KEY. If both are present precedence is different. If only REDWOOD_API_KEY exists Node SDK mistakenly reads cached REDWOOD_TOKEN from process.env at startup (race with our CLI who writes to ~/.redwood/creds).

samir: repro script attached: 
```
# reproduce
rm -f ~/.redwood/creds
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_live_newyyy
node sampleapp/index.js
```

carla: can you paste the minimal stack trace? also which CLI version? I think a recent change to the credential-resolver caused the startup cache to not re-check env after reading disk.

samir: CLI v1.8.2. Stack: `AuthError -> fetch -> index.js:42`. Short term workaround: `unset REDWOOD_TOKEN` before starting sampleapp and it works.

ops-alex: :facepalm: that explains why our canary in dedicated hit auth failures during key rotation last week. The rotation process writes a new token file and then updates env via systemd drop-ins on our test env — race condition.

jlee: proposed fixes: 1) Make resolver re-check env vars with higher priority on each request (cheap check) 2) Add a one-time warning if REDWOOD_TOKEN and REDWOOD_API_KEY mismatch at startup 3) Normalize accepted env var names in all SDKs to REDWOOD_API_KEY and deprecate others with clear warnings and migration docs.

carla: agree. Also add an opt-in fallback env var list but log which name was used. Developers keep having both names around because earlier examples used different names in sampleapps.

devex-bot: Reminder: please file a follow-up GH issue in repo redwood/sdk-credential-resolver and tag @eng-runtime and @devex.

samir: created issue #1234 and linked repro steps + logs. I also pushed a tiny fix to my branch that unsets any cached token if REDWOOD_API_KEY changes at runtime. Patch link: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-cred/commit/abcdef

jlee: nice. Can you open a PR with tests? Cover scenarios: env-only, disk-only, both present (mismatched), rotation (env changed while process running).

samir: will do. For the sampleapp docs: we should standardize examples to always use `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and a short note about rotation: 
```
# rotate keys safely (sampleapp)
# 1) update key in secrets manager
# 2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newkey
# 3) restart process OR send SIGHUP to reload creds
```

carla: also add an onboarding warning in the CLI when it writes creds: "If you previously used REDWOOD_TOKEN, consider migrating to REDWOOD_API_KEY — see docs link". That should reduce future confusion.

ops-alex: I'll coordinate a small runbook for Dedicated customers to avoid ephemeral mixups during org-level rotations.

jlee: final plan: samir opens PR + tests; carla will draft deprecation note and docs patch; ops-alex will update runbook; devex-bot will triage issue to eng-runtime. Target: patch cut in next minor (v1.9.0) and docs updated same week.

samir: thanks all — quick win was adding a debug log that prints which env var was used (masked) so users see it. Pushed to branch.

carla: :thumbsup: follow-up: let's also add an integration test in sampleapp CI that simulates a rotation and asserts no 401s.

samir: on it, will pair with @jlee tomorrow to cover tests.
